claim: vars = refIds.map((v) => v.value!) uses a non-null assertion, so vars[0] is undefined when refIds is empty (SQL expression is the only query); quoteIdentifierIfNecessary then reaches identifier.toUpperCase() in isValidIdentifier (mysql/sqlUtil.ts:54) and throws TypeError in the render body, unmounting the editor subtree. Probe-verified as a change-introduced regression — the old code degraded to the harmless text 'FROM undefined'.

claim: The change imports the shared mysql quoteIdentifierIfNecessary into SqlExpr.tsx and sqlCompletionProvider.ts but not into metaSqlExpr.ts, so metaSqlExpr.ts:15 silently resolves to that file's own regex-only copy at :114 which omits the RESERVED_WORDS check; a reserved-word RefID (Order, Group, select) is quoted in the editor query and completion but left unquoted in the metadata query, producing a backend syntax error.

claim: Completions now insert backtick-quoted table names, but the expressions provider supplies no parseName, so plugin-ui's defaultTableNameParser returns the lone backtick token (monaco emits identifier.quote separately); fetchSQLFields then re-quotes it and queries.filter((q) => q.refId === query.table) matches no frame, and the failure is swallowed by the bare catch at sqlCompletionProvider.ts:38-40 so column autocomplete silently returns nothing. Sibling mssql/postgres providers supply a custom parseName.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: Completions now insert backtick-quoted table names, but the read path never unquotes them — column autocomplete silently returns nothing for exactly the names this change targets

claim: Neither quoteIdentifierIfNecessary implementation doubles backticks embedded in the value, as MySQL identifier quoting requires; a RefID like A`,`B yields FROM `A`,`B`, terminating its own quoting so the rest parses as query structure. The change makes this helper the sole sanitization step on three generated-SQL paths, one of which builds SQL the user never sees. (security-reviewer rated this High as an injection surface; the orchestrator lowered it to Low, unable to substantiate a crossed trust boundary.)
